name: 2027 code-ready adaptation — v3
assumptions: 2027 planning proposal, version 3, Foundation revision 2, based on capability model 2 revision 3 and catalogue v11 assessed on 18 October 2026. Foundation is shared knowledge; L1-L3 describe work with AI, while role responsibilities and approved product access are independent. Full-course durations are counted; ranges use their upper bound. The shared course budgets are 2h Foundation, 2h L1, 8h L2 and 24h L3. Foundation uses the 1h45 AI-literacy course; INT-2787 is excluded as excessive depth for this audience. Social engineering and deepfakes receive a 10-minute awareness segment within the existing bank session, with no added internal hours. Role course budgets are provisionally 4h; architecture is 4.25h and BISO 5h. Internal learner hours are additional and proposed; they earn no syllabus-score credit. Headcounts, licences, platform approval, coach capacity and learner prerequisites require owner validation. No operational authorisation or competence is implied by coverage. Global scope excludes TR-125/TR-128/TR-129; TR-159 is excluded until its lab bundle is scoped. Existing duration overrides are retained for comparable full-resource estimates; TR-118 is a 6h reading-bundle estimate and TR-155 a 9h26m path. The v10 evidence is archived; unchanged outcomes retain their assessments. V11 must-have review: N5.1 merges deepfake impersonation, N5.8 adds a separate Foundation cyber risk overview, N5.4 retains bank attack examples. Core flags and four changed outcomes are reassessed. Automated-judge validation is essential for the L3 route using judges; AI-assisted assurance is essential for BISO using AI in assurance. Identity delegation protocol depth belongs to integration. Other course budgets are retained; the new 45-minute internal risk overview is explicit additional learner time and earns no assessed credit. Coding adaptation: replace Build with Andrew with the complete 2h Claude Code course for learners already familiar with Python/Git and with an approved environment. All internal safe-use practice remains. No assumption of organisation-wide Claude Code access.

cohorts.name: Foundation — common knowledge

internal.title: AI in our cyber work: colleague showcase
internal.outcomes: Explain one own-domain and one adjacent-domain case, limits and changed human work.

internal.title: Approved platform, architecture and safe use
internal.outcomes: Trace a request across model, tools and data; choose safe inputs and identify the accountable owner.

internal.title: AI limitations, bank attack examples and knowledge check
internal.outcomes: Recognise unsupported output and suspicious content, explain uncertainty, identify the bank attack scenario and choose independent trusted-channel verification or escalation.

internal.title: Overview of AI security risks
internal.owner: Cyber awareness lead + AI security architect
internal.outcomes: Learner categorises short scenarios, explains the consequence and selects the appropriate precaution/escalation. Pilot and assess the module against N5.8 before awarding coverage credit.

cohorts.rationale: Assign the 1h45 AI-literacy course within a 2h Foundation course budget. Social engineering and deepfake impersonation need a brief awareness treatment for cyber staff: use a 10-minute segment within the existing bank session for recognition, independent trusted-channel verification and escalation. Do not assign the full INT-2787 social-engineering course to Foundation. Keep N5.8 risk overview separate from N5.4 bank attack examples. Proposed internal learning remains unassessed.
cohorts.note: Everyone: common knowledge, including bank-approved uses, limitations, responsible use and AI-enabled threats.
